prompt_text: Who is the best interior painting company in St. Louis MO?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t one objectively “best” interior painting company for all jobs in St. Louis — the right company depends on your home, budget, timeline and the level of prep/finish you want. I can help you find a good match. First, here are practical steps, criteria and red flags to guide your choice.

How to find the best painter for you
- Search local review sites and forums: Google Reviews, Yelp, Angi, Houzz, BBB, Nextdoor, and local Facebook groups.  
- Ask neighbors and real-estate agents for recommendations and to see finished work in person.  
- Get at least 3 written estimates for the exact scope (prep, repairs, number of coats, trim/doors, ceilings).  
- Compare apples to apples: brand/finish of paint, number of coats, patching/plaster work, cleanup, and warranty.

Questions to ask every contractor
- Are you licensed, insured and bonded? (Ask for COI.)  
- Do you have references or photos of recent interior work? Can I visit a job?  
- Do you have EPA RRP (lead-safe) certification for homes built before 1978?  
- Who will do the work — employees or subcontractors? Will the same crew be on site?  
- What paint brands and sheen do you use? Are samples included?  
- What is the timeline, payment schedule, and warranty?  
- How do you handle damage, touch-ups, and clean-up?

What to look for in reviews and bids
- Consistently positive comments on punctuality, prep work, and clean edges.  
- Clear written contract that lists all inclusions.  
- Reasonable, not the cheapest, estimate — very low bids often mean corners cut.  
- Willingness to do a walk-through and provide a punch-list when finished.

Typical cost ballpark (very approximate)
- Many interior jobs fall roughly between $2–$6 per square foot of painted surface or $300–$1,200+ per room depending on size, ceilings, repair work and paint quality. Get written estimates for your specific project.

Red flags
- No references or online presence, demands large upfront payment, refuses a written contract, or gives a vague scope of work.

If you want, I can:
- Narrow candidates to top-rated local painters near you if you give your ZIP code or neighborhood and tell me the size/nature of the job (single room vs whole house, ceilings, trim, repairs, timeline, budget).
- Provide a templated list of questions and a contract checklist you can use when getting bids.

Which would you prefer — help finding specific companies nearby, or a checklist/estimate template to use when you call painters?
